newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian Sugar-Thai premiums ease as supplies grow.
newsitem.headline: Asian Sugar-Thai premiums ease as supplies grow.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums have fallen slightly since rain in sugar growing areas in Thailand eased the tight supply situation, Japanese traders said on Friday.
Thai premiums had until recently firmed on concerns that an unseasonable dry spell in Thailand would damage crops and tighten supplies.

On Friday, Thai raw sugar premiums for July-September deliveries were quoted at around 85/90 points (bid/offer) per pound over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange futures on an fob basis, compared to 90/100 a week earlier.
"Premiums eased slightly following rain there. But the fundamentals will remain bullish," a sugar trader at a major trade house said.
The Tokyo raw sugar futures market gained across the board during the Friday morning session, due to the New York market's price gains and the weaker yen against the dollar, traders said.

The benchmark January 1999 contract was up 800 yen at 30,210 yen per tonne at the close of morning session. "A local brokerage house built large long positions in nearby months," a brokerage house trader said.
Japan's raw sugar imports totalled 151,904 tonnes in June, down by 8.16 percent from the same month a year earlier, Finance Ministry data showed on Tuesday.
Total imports in the first six months of calendar 1997 reached 738,560 tonnes, against 740,465 tonnes during the same period last year.
